# Error tables

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_table.py from data/error-bounds.json -- do not edit by hand. -->

Every bound in this file and in `include/ulpgrad/tables.h` comes from one
measurement, and the same measurement produces both: change a coefficient and
the numbers move together, or they do not move at all.

| step | file |
|---|---|
| golden reference | `data/reference/exp.csv`, `data/reference/exp2.csv`, `data/reference/log.csv`, `data/reference/log1p.csv`, `data/reference/log2.csv`, `data/reference/rsqrt.csv`, `data/reference/tanh.csv` |
| reference arithmetic | `experiments/m3_fit/gen_golden.py`, mpmath at 40 digits, direct RNE |
| the run being measured | `tools/measure_bounds.cpp`, this build |
| measured numbers | `data/error-bounds.json` |
| declared numbers | `include/ulpgrad/tables.h`, this file |
| tests that keep them honest | `tests/test_exp.cpp`, `tests/test_log.cpp`, `tests/test_rsqrt.cpp`, `tests/test_tanh.cpp`, `tests/test_special_cases.cpp`, `tests/test_table_freshness.cpp` |

## Measurement environment

| item | value |
|---|---|
| date | Nov 15 2026 |
| OS / arch | Windows / x64 |
| CPU | Intel64 Family 6 Model 158 Stepping 10, GenuineIntel |
| compiler | MSVC 35229 |

The ULP distance is computed on the monotone integer image of the bit
pattern (`ulp_distance` in `include/ulpgrad/detail/bits.h`), so `+0` and
`-0` are 0 ULP apart and adjacent floats are 1 apart across zero, across the
subnormal boundary and across the infinities. A NaN pattern has no position
on that order, so every comparison that involves one is done bit for bit
instead: the NaN an argument carries, and the NaN a domain contract returns
for a real argument, such as `log(-1)`.

## `exp`

| metric | value |
|---|---|
| points in the golden file | 9,334 |
| points carrying a ULP distance | 9,331 |
| NaN inputs, checked bit for bit | 3 (0 mismatches) |
| NaN results for a real argument | 0 |
| **max ULP** | **1** |
| exactly rounded | 94.81 % |
| worst input | `0x41907302` |
| reference | mpmath 1.4.1 at 40 decimal digits, direct round-to-nearest-even to float32 |
| sample seed | `0x5EED0003` |

| `\|x\|` | points | max ULP | exactly rounded |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| [0, 1) | 672 | 1 | 98.66 % |
| [1, 2) | 176 | 1 | 92.61 % |
| [2, 4) | 337 | 1 | 94.07 % |
| [4, 8) | 696 | 1 | 93.53 % |
| [8, 16) | 1,310 | 1 | 95.42 % |
| [16, 32) | 2,529 | 1 | 94.66 % |
| [32, 64) | 1,790 | 1 | 94.53 % |
| [64, inf) | 1,821 | 1 | 94.29 % |

The maximum is 1 ULP in the worst bucket and 1 ULP overall: the error
does not grow with the argument.
The rounding of the reference is done on the significand, never through
`double`, which would round twice and disagree on exact ties.
